evidence.summary: Controlled observations showed a positive relationship between age and score in the tested regions.
Controlled observations showed a positive relationship between prior visits and score in the tested regions.
In a controlled configuration, reducing years_registered from 40 to 0 increased the score by approximately 0.10, indicating a negative relationship in that tested region.
Controlled observations showed substantial score changes associated with comorbidity_ratio, with the magnitude depending on the surrounding configuration.
Changing ward produced smaller score differences in the tested configurations.
The highest observed DECLINE score was 0.4522 and the lowest observed APPROVE score was 0.4937. Their midpoint, approximately 0.4729, was used as the surrogate decision cutoff.
An Extra Trees surrogate trained on 90 Round-1 and Round-2 observations achieved 82.5% decision accuracy, MAE 0.1193 and R² 0.1713 on 80 unseen Round-4 queries.
